## What Changed

**`src/cache.js`** — added an in-flight promise map alongside the value cache:
- `get(key)` returns the cached value if present.
- Otherwise the first caller creates a single shared promise, stores it in `inFlight`, and every concurrent caller for that key awaits that same promise.
- On success the value is written to `values` so it's kept.
- The in-flight entry is removed when the promise settles (with an identity check so a newer load can't be deleted), so a failed load is not kept and the next `get` retries.
- Synchronous loader throws are also normalized to a rejected promise.
- Every waiting caller receives the same resolution or rejection.

**`cache.test.js`** — added two tests before implementing: one for a shared failed load that is retried by the next get, and one confirming loaded values are kept.

## Evidence

RED run before the fix:
```
✖ concurrent gets of one key load once — actual 3, expected 1
✖ a failed concurrent load is shared and retried on the next get
ℹ pass 1, fail 2
```

GREEN run after the fix:
```
✔ concurrent gets of one key load once
✔ a failed concurrent load is shared and retried on the next get
✔ a loaded value is kept
ℹ pass 3, fail 0
EXIT: 0
```

Project verification: `kriya_verify` → **passes** (`node --test`, exit 0), session verdict: verified.

## Why

Caching the *promise* rather than only the resolved value makes concurrent `get`s coalesce naturally, and deferring the value write to `.then` keeps a rejected load out of the cache. Cleanup on settle, guarded by identity, preserves retry semantics without racing a replacement load.

Fixed and verified.

**Root cause:** In `src/tokenize.js`, the quoted-string loop was `while (text[i] !== '"')` with no end-of-input bound. For an unterminated quote, `text[i]` remains `undefined` forever, so the condition never becomes false and the loop never terminates.

**Fix** (`src/tokenize.js`):
```js
while (i < text.length && text[i] !== '"') {
  if (text[i] === "\\" && text[i + 1] === '"') i++
  word += text[i]
  i++
}
if (i >= text.length) throw new SyntaxError("Unterminated quote")
i++
```

This also handles a trailing backslash inside a quoted string, which previously would have run off the end as well.

**Verification:**
- `node --test` → 2 passed, 0 failed. The formerly hanging `echo "oops` case now returns `SyntaxError` in ~21ms.
- Edge cases checked: empty input, whitespace-only, quoted groups, escaped quotes, trailing backslash, and unterminated quotes in the middle/end of input.
